summary: Pick a value, or a span of values, where the approximate position matters more than the number.

pairs.dont: Ship a slider with no readout of the value it is setting.
pairs.do: Put the number beside it, or let a field mirror it.
pairs.why: A thumb on a track is an approximation. Anyone who needs the exact figure — and in a threshold they always do — cannot get it from the position.

pairs.dont: Use a slider to enter a port number or a timeout in milliseconds.
pairs.do: Use a slider for ranges people judge by feel; use a number input for exact values.
pairs.why: Hitting one value in a thousand by dragging is a pointer-accuracy test, and it is much worse on a touchscreen.

pairs.dont: Leave a range slider's two thumbs unlabelled.
pairs.why: A screen reader announces two controls both called "slider", with no way to tell which end is which.

pairs.dont: Leave step at 1 on a 0–10000 range.
pairs.do: Set a step that matches the precision the value actually has.
pairs.why: Ten thousand keyboard presses to cross the track is not keyboard support.

pairs.dont: Leave a disabled slider looking exactly like a live one.
pairs.why: The file draws them identically today. People drag a control that cannot move and conclude the page is broken.

a11y: Radix supplies role="slider", the aria-value* attributes and arrow, Page and Home/End keys on every thumb.
A range slider has two thumbs and therefore needs two names: pass thumbLabels, or both announce the same thing.
Disabled removes the hover and focus effects as well as the pointer. A disabled control that still looks live is the same defect as one that looks disabled and is not.
